summary: Codegen-depth IR test for bigint retain/release is entirely absent, though named in #624's acceptance criteria and the plan's 5.4/5.5
note: Verified independently: grep for bigint_retain|bigint_release|bigint_rc across tests/ returns zero matches; the convention exists as tests/slice1_codegen_depth.rs and tests/container_methods1_codegen_depth.rs. The new test file is CLI/black-box plus the cfg(unix) RSS oracle; nothing inspects emitted IR, so the inline tag-check guard ordering and the phi-predecessor safety of the block-splitting emit_bigint_refcount_call were confirmed only by manual audit, not by a repeatable gate. FIX LANDED IN-CRATE, not under tests/: compile_to_object_with_observer is private, so tests/slice1_codegen_depth.rs's hand-built-MIR route cannot inspect real emitted IR. Followed the in-crate convention of an_oversized_int_literal_materializes_a_runtime_bigint instead, asserting a full guard-dominance chain per refcount call. A follow-up reviewer round then caught a real defect in that helper: LLVM disambiguates SSA names per function, so the defs/branches maps had to be reset per `define` or a call could be validated against a guard chain from a different function.

summary: AttrSet comment claims the bool-into-int-attribute leak is pinned by a test that only covers a plain local, not an attribute
note: Verified independently: the cited test a_bool_assigned_into_a_bigint_valued_int_slot_releases_the_old_word uses 'x: int = PROMOTED; x = True' (a local slot via release_int_slot_before_store, gated on the slot's declared Ty), whereas the comment describes release_int_attr_slot_before_store, gated on value_ty. grep for 'self.' in tests/issue_146_bigint_release.rs returns zero fixtures. Behavior itself is leak-only and correctly recorded as D-180 Consequences item 6; the defect is the coverage claim.

summary: A new test helper called inkwell's `module.verify()` directly, bypassing the crate's own `#[cfg(windows)]`-skipped `verify_module` wrapper, and crashed the whole Windows test binary with STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION
note: D-029: inkwell's LLVMString Drop calls LLVMDisposeMessage, which faults against the prebuilt LLVM 22.1.1 the Windows runner uses -- and Module::verify takes that path on its SUCCESS branch too, not only on error. The crate already owns a Windows-safe wrapper (`verify_module`, a no-op under `#[cfg(windows)]`); the new test reached past it to the raw inkwell API. Fixed by deleting the call outright: `compile_to_object_with_observer` already runs `verify_module` on the same module BEFORE invoking the observer, so the guarantee was never lost. Standing blind spot this exposes: no local gate on macOS/Linux can catch this class -- the Windows job runs single-threaded specifically because of D-029, so any new inkwell-touching test ships untested until CI runs. Mechanically guardable: grep for a direct `module.verify()` or any inkwell API returning an LLVMString that is not routed through `llvm_string_to_owned`, outside the two wrapper definitions themselves.
